After food.

A common blood test that counts the different types of cells in your blood: red cells, white cells and platelets.
Measures haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body. A low level can be a sign of anaemia.

aliases: WCC|WBC|White blood cell count|White blood count
definition: Counts the white blood cells, which help your body fight infection.
Counts platelets, the small blood cells that help your blood clot and stop bleeding.
Counts the red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
Measures how much of your blood is made up of red blood cells.
Measures the average size of your red blood cells.
Counts neutrophils, the most common type of white blood cell, which fight bacterial infections.
Counts lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell that helps fight viral infections.
A group of blood tests that check salts in your blood (such as sodium and potassium) and how well your kidneys are working.
Measures sodium, a salt your body needs to balance fluids and help nerves and muscles work.
Measures potassium, a mineral that helps your heart, nerves and muscles work properly.
Measures urea, a waste product your kidneys remove from the blood. It helps show how well your kidneys are working.
Measures creatinine, a waste product from your muscles that your kidneys filter out. It helps show how well your kidneys are working.
An estimate of how well your kidneys filter waste from your blood, worked out from your creatinine result.
A group of blood tests that check how well your liver is working.
Measures ALT, an enzyme found mostly in the liver. High levels can be a sign of liver irritation or damage.
Measures AST, an enzyme found in the liver and muscles. High levels can be a sign of liver or muscle damage.
Measures ALP, an enzyme found mainly in the liver and bones.
Measures GGT, an enzyme found mostly in the liver. It is often checked with other liver tests.
Measures bilirubin, a yellow substance made when old red blood cells are broken down. The liver normally clears it.
Measures albumin, a protein made by the liver that helps keep fluid in your blood vessels.
Measures the total amount of cholesterol, a fatty substance, in your blood.
Measures LDL, often called bad cholesterol, which can build up in the walls of blood vessels.
Measures HDL, often called good cholesterol, which helps remove other cholesterol from the blood.
Measures triglycerides, a type of fat in your blood.
Measures the amount of sugar (glucose) in your blood at the time of the test.
Shows your average blood sugar level over the past two to three months.
Measures TSH, a hormone that tells your thyroid gland how much thyroid hormone to make. It is used to check how well your thyroid is working.
Measures thyroxine (T4), the main hormone made by your thyroid gland.
Measures CRP, a protein made by the liver. The level goes up when there is inflammation or infection in the body.
Measures how quickly red blood cells settle in a tube. A faster rate can be a sign of inflammation.
Measures ferritin, a protein that stores iron. It shows how much iron your body has stored.
Measures vitamin B12, which your body needs to make red blood cells and keep nerves healthy.
Measures folate, a B vitamin your body needs to make healthy red blood cells.
Measures vitamin D, which helps keep your bones and muscles healthy.

aliases: International normalised ratio|International normalized ratio|PT/INR|Prothrombin time
definition: Measures how long your blood takes to clot. It is often used to check blood-thinning medicine such as warfarin.
Measures calcium, a mineral needed for strong bones and for nerves, muscles and the heart to work.
Measures magnesium, a mineral that helps your muscles, nerves and heart work.
Measures phosphate, a mineral that works with calcium to build strong bones and teeth.
Measures troponin, a protein released into the blood when the heart muscle is damaged.
Measures PSA, a protein made by the prostate gland.
Measures uric acid, a waste product in the blood. High levels can lead to gout.
Measures creatine kinase, an enzyme released into the blood when muscles are damaged.
A vaccine that protects against three infections: diphtheria, tetanus and whooping cough (pertussis).
A booster vaccine for older children and adults that protects against tetanus, diphtheria and whooping cough.
A booster vaccine that protects against tetanus and diphtheria.
A combined baby vaccine that protects against six infections: diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib and hepatitis B.
A vaccine that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (German measles).
A vaccine that protects against Hib bacteria, which can cause meningitis and other serious infections in young children.
A vaccine that protects against polio.
A vaccine that protects against hepatitis B, a virus that infects the liver.
A vaccine that protects against HPV, a virus that can cause some cancers and genital warts.
A vaccine that protects against meningococcal B bacteria, a cause of meningitis and blood poisoning (sepsis).
A vaccine that protects against meningococcal C bacteria, a cause of meningitis and sepsis.
A vaccine that protects against four types of meningococcal bacteria (A, C, W and Y), a cause of meningitis and sepsis.
A vaccine that protects against pneumococcal bacteria, a cause of pneumonia, meningitis and ear infections.
A vaccine for older adults and people at higher risk that protects against 23 types of pneumococcal bacteria.
A vaccine given by mouth to babies that protects against rotavirus, a common cause of severe diarrhoea and vomiting.
A vaccine that protects against tuberculosis (TB), a bacterial infection that mainly affects the lungs.
A yearly vaccine that protects against the flu virus.
A vaccine that protects against chickenpox.
A vaccine for older adults that protects against shingles, a painful rash caused by the chickenpox virus waking up again.
A vaccine that protects against serious illness from COVID-19.
